findings: Read all nineteen source pages, all common and application proofs, both full GAP files and the two Lean statements. Principal scope is source Theorem4.1: cases1/2 with exactly their hypotheses, case3 explicitly refuted and replaced by an iff, both end-group C properties, full Lemma5.3 and the three finite Section6 examples. The introductory Table1 remains retained motivating census data, not a regenerated classification.

The basic hypotheses themselves force the anchored H-orbit to be the union of two different B-components, at least one a triple. A triple has one b-fixed vertex. If neither component is a triple then c fixes the entire union and transitivity forces c=1. This supplies sizes4/5/6 without importing the source cases, so the full block lemma applies before selecting a case.

The dihedral stabilizer argument is valid for the actual permutation action: B is D6 or D12, with triple kernel generated by z=(ab)^3. A reflection cannot fix two successive points of a rotation orbit of length at least3. Centrality plus one fixed point in a transitive action excludes the unwanted z. For the H end, fixing u alone forces the exponent divisible by3 or4; this was clarified in the additive edition, avoiding the unjustified earlier wording about already fixing the whole left pair.

The normal closure of t gives actual supported Sym(O) for sizes4/5 and the three matching flips N for size6. The complementary restriction of each B-element can then be isolated, proving the direct or semidirect factorizations. These are full subgroup equalities, not inferences from abstract group orders.

The block argument checks every B-triple: a triple in one block would force a second block swapped by c, both preserved by a,b; their union would be the whole K-orbit, contradicting an anchored c-fixed point. Discrete separation and an additional point in the anchor block give a second triple in matching blocks. This proves both source Lemma5.3 conclusions without the long propagation cases.

For sizes4/5, subtracting the common complementary restriction reduces H intersection K to a permutation supported on O. A companion triple fixes its three block actions; parity removes the remaining left-pair flip in size5. The vacuous-imprimitivity boundary is handled separately by centrality of a_out; the explicit order12 even-subgroup argument completes size5. No extra hypothesis is hidden.

For size6, the uniformly proved two ends and the end criterion leave exactly N intersection K=1, hence seven actual membership tests. Distinct K-orbits of the two triples suffice. In the accepted eighteen-point example all seven nonidentity matching elements belong to K; the unrestricted source conclusion is false.

Root independent GAP code imports no author implementation. It checks the three literal original symmetric groups, their rank-three end intersections, actual supported direct factors and explicit failed-output elements; all source orders and actions agree. The inherited counterexample separately gives the exact normal closure N of order8, trivial N intersection B and H=N*B, with all seven obstructions in K. The complete old192 parabolic checks are supplied by the fresh root invocation of the author program, not misreported as independently rewritten here.
